Law 8b removal test passes: remove storage (the system retaining retrievable information in a durable substrate) and dark-data cannot exist. Its accepted definition carves it as information that is 'collected, stores, and possesses but cannot access, use, or analyze', and it explicitly distinguishes itself from missing data ('data that does not exist') precisely by being stored-but-inaccessible. Every cited instance — email archives, legacy database dumps, unindexed documents, encrypted drives — is stored information; the removal of storage removes the persistence that constitutes the kind. Not identity (dark-data is a category of information, not the storage system) and not purpose: a genuine constitutive dependency, analogous to the accepted semitone DEPENDS_ON pitch.

Law 8d (for whose sake?): ZPD's own accepted definition carves it as a construct 'used in educational theory to define the space where learning occurs' — it maps a developmental-capacity space; its master is the learning space it delineates, not the transmission practice. The note's pinned sense overreaches: 'only defined in relation to instructional guidance' is false under the from-side's definition — its parameters (independent level, assisted level, scaffold) are supplied by 'a more knowledgeable person', which includes peers and collaborators, not the teaching institution. And the note's removal test ('remove teaching and ZPD loses its entire meaning') fails: ZPD retains full meaning in dynamic assessment, peer scaffolding, and developmental research. A construct persisting 'through pedagogical practice' has pedagogy as a persistence mechanism, not as its beneficiary.

Explanatory dependence is not operational dependence (Laws 2b/8b). The note's own load-bearing clause says interleaving would "lose its explanatory mechanism" if cognitive-load-theory were removed — an explanation, not an operation. The technique's operation is behavioral: present mixed problem types, force discrimination, select strategies. It operates in mathematics, music, and sports training (per its accepted definition) with or without anyone knowing Sweller's framework; the technique predates and is independently practiced apart from CLT, and its credited mechanism in its own definition is discrimination and retrieval practice, not load classification. Removing the theory does not stop the practice operating; at most one candidate account of why it works is removed. If anything, the honest relation is DERIVED_FROM-grade (the technique's research literature draws on load theory), not DEPENDS_ON.

A mark is not an instance of its craft (Law 9a: a topic is not an instance of its discipline). Typography's accepted definition carves a CRAFT — "the craft of designing the visual arrangement of written text" with parameters like typeface family, leading, kerning, margin proportions. A diacritic is a mark: its accepted definition carves "a mark or symbol added to a letter or character… a secondary graphic element superimposed on a base glyph." The note even pins the right thing — "a specific kind of TYPGRAPHIC MARK" — and then files the mark against the craft. The nearest accepted kind for the pinned mark-sense is glyph ("a visually distinct character, mark, or symbol that functions as a unit within a writing system"; a combining diacritic is literally a glyph), and diacritic's accepted kind-edge is already seated: diacritic INSTANCE_OF symbol. Filing INSTANCE_OF typography confuses the object with the activity that arranges it.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): "a short, memorable phrase repeated by a character or entity, becoming widely associated with them." Phrase's accepted definition: a group of words forming a single unit of meaning within a larger syntactic structure. A catchphrase is exactly such a unit — its own accepted definition opens "a self-contained linguistic unit — a phrase, clause, or single line — constructed for high memorability and rapid cultural transmission." The defining parameter that distinguishes it (association + repetition + detachable context) is added to the phrase base, not substituted for it. Nearest-kind (Laws 9/11e): idiom is NOT the kind — idiom's carve is semantic opacity (meaning non-compositional), while a catchphrase's meaning is typically compositional ("Bye, Felicia"); idiom is a sibling leaf, not a parent. No other accepted kind sits between; catchphrase's existing accepted edges (INSTANCE_OF language, INSTANCE_OF expression) do not make phrase derivable, and phrase itself sits under the same expression umbrella, so the rung completes the structure rather than leaping it.

The note conflates the bar with the bar LINE (Law 11d sense-pin against the accepted carve). bar's accepted definition carves a UNIT OF MUSICAL TIME: "a unit of musical time… containing exactly the number of beats specified by the time signature. It segments musical rhythm into regularly recurring temporal units, enabling performers to navigate complex rhythms through structural grouping," persisting through "Western music notation conventions, pedagogical practice, and PERFORMANCE TRADITION." Removal test (Law 8b): remove the staff now — does the measure stop operating? No. The measure as a temporal grouping of beats operates in performance (performers count bars with no notation at all), in pedagogy, and in other notations; its operational substrate is the beat and the time signature, not five parallel lines. What genuinely depends on the staff are the MARKS drawn on it — and the board already seats those: barline DEPENDS_ON staff, note DEPENDS_ON staff, rest DEPENDS_ON staff, clef DEPENDS_ON staff, all ACCEPTED. "Beats are positioned relative to staff lines/spaces" is pitch placement, not what makes a bar a bar. The honest dependency is the one already on the board: bar DERIVED_FROM musical-notation.

Part-and-whole (Law 10) in the pinned sense: "beats are literal temporal parts contained within the bar's span." bar's accepted definition states the measure "contains exactly the number of beats specified by the time signature"; beat's accepted definition is "a regularly recurring pulse of emphasis in time, the temporal unit that organizes rhythmic experience" — the metronomic backbone of meter. The measure is the whole composed of its beats as temporal parts (a 4/4 bar's span is constituted by its four beats), and the board already treats the beat as the temporal substrate of this cluster: meter DEPENDS_ON beat is ACCEPTED. Removing the beats would leave the measure an empty span with no constituent units — the whole loses its parts. CONTAINS, whole to part, holds in the pinned sense.

payload.scope: A human-made musical construct: a set of two or more pitches sounded simultaneously, whose members bear harmonic relations to one another, built to persist as a fundamental unit of Western harmony through theoretical analysis, performance practice, notation, and teaching.

payload.body: A chord is a human-made musical construct: a set of two or more pitches (notes) sounded simultaneously, whose members bear harmonic relations to one another. Parameters: (1) size — the number of constituent pitches: dyad (two), triad (three), seventh chord (four), ninth chord (five) and beyond; (2) quality — the intervallic structure among the members: major (root–major third–perfect fifth), minor (root–minor third–perfect fifth), diminished (root–minor third–diminished fifth), augmented (root–major third–augmented fifth); (3) inversion — the arrangement of the members by which a different member occupies the bass position, changing the surface harmony while preserving the chord's identity; (4) voicing — the specific octave placement and spacing of the members, which affects the chord's texture without changing its harmonic function. Persistence mechanism: standardized in Western music theory through harmonic analysis, taught in harmony and ear-training curricula, reproduced in performance practice through chord symbols in lead sheets and jazz charts, and maintained through the notation of figured bass and the modern chord symbol system (e.g., 'Cmaj7', 'Am7b5'). It is distinguished from a single note (which fixes one pitch; the chord fixes a set), from a scale (which organizes pitches sequentially into a framework; the chord presents them simultaneously), and from a melody (which unfolds pitches in time; the chord suspends them together). [formal: chorda | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
